proposed_from.topic: Close the full two-nuisance structure-agnostic minimax gap for the partially linear causal coefficient: match Gu–Yin–Cai–Fan Appendix A.1 with a budget-aware two-sided empirical-balancing estimator, or prove the missing cross-stochastic lower bound
proposed_from.novelty_justification: The proposal isolates the missing fixed-class product converse in an identified mean-zero PLM rather than silently correcting the literal Appendix A.1 model. In the asymmetric regime, the paper's displayed upper expression has product order while its displayed lower expression is asymptotically smaller. Conditional on confirmation of the apparent typographical error, the proposed open question strictly tightens that lower benchmark; without confirmation, its advance is a new closely motivated fixed-class mean-zero experiment. It makes no claim in the already terminal regime \(s_{\pi,n}\ge s_{\mu,n}\).

seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Jin and Syrgkanis because their PLM mixed-bias lower bound already multiplies two nuisance tolerances.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their result is an approximation-tolerance mixed-bias construction; it does not preserve two localized stochastic budgets or establish the Appendix A.1 all-estimator product.
seed_details.burned_reason: The universal fixed-class cross-stochastic product converse collapses on the allowed degenerate-covariate subclass; the surviving root-n counterexample is incremental rather than field-level.

seed_details.red_team: A two-sided balance program is a routine duplication of one-sided SADE.
seed_details.rebuttal: The unresolved fold-conditional empirical process contains both random nuisance channels, so the one-sided multiplier argument does not control the new remainder.

seed_details.red_team: Nested sample splitting and aggregation make adaptation routine.
seed_details.rebuttal: The selector must distinguish unobserved approximation from stochastic budgets without losing the term it is selecting over.

seed_details.red_team: DML Wald inference applies once a point-risk bound is known.
seed_details.rebuttal: Frontier bias can be of sampling order and the active rule switches across regimes, neither covered by the DML negligible-product expansion.

seed_details.red_team: Higher-order orthogonality already answers the question off Gaussianity.
seed_details.rebuttal: Existing cumulant results do not combine local-to-Gaussian cumulants with two learner approximation and stochastic budgets.

seed_details.red_team: The upper-bound minimum already displays the frontier.
seed_details.rebuttal: A displayed oracle minimum is not a derived observed-primitives equivalence and divergence frontier.

seed_details.red_team: Efficiency is only regular after the minimax remainder is negligible.
seed_details.rebuttal: No nonregular efficiency notion is specified by the current substrate.

seed_details.red_team: The substrate has a fixed coefficient target and supplies neither a policy class nor a valid finite-sample symmetry group.
seed_details.rebuttal: No credible native policy-regret or permutation-inversion kernel was found; these lanes are not padded.

proposed_from.literature_map: Gu et al. \cite{gu2026optimally} solve the one-learnable-nuisance problem with SADE, then state the nonmatching two-nuisance Appendix A.1 frontier. Gu \cite{gu2025open} isolates variance propagation as the PLM structure-agnostic obstruction. Chernozhukov et al. \cite{chernozhukov2018dml} provide the orthogonal-score product-remainder benchmark. Hirshberg and Wager \cite{hirshberg2021augmented} provide empirical bias--variance balancing and conditional linearization, but not this four-budget minimax experiment. Balakrishnan et al. \cite{balakrishnan2023fundamental} formalize generic structure-agnostic lower bounds. Jin and Syrgkanis \cite{jin2025sharp} supply the closest technique: sequential, PLM-preserving fuzzy hypotheses that generate mixed-bias separation, but their published theorem does not incorporate two localized stochastic radii.

accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The mean-zero fixed-class converse is the claim under review; its status as a strict tightening of Gu et al.'s literal Appendix A.1 lower display is assumed only if the authors confirm that E[epsilon Y|X,T]=0 is a typographical error.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: A product converse for m_PL^0 is a conditional claim on the explicitly defined mean-zero experiment; comparison as a strict tightening of gu2026optimally Theorem A.1 is conditional on source correction, otherwise it is a closely motivated distinct experiment.

banked_reason: The standard one-regressor root-n reduction at degenerate X is mathematically sound but does not close or refute Gu et al.'s two-nuisance gap at field tier.
